name: Best Buy Co., Inc.
executive_summary: Best Buy Co., Inc. (BBY) screens as a **strong buy** on quantitative value metrics (11/22 models; composite 77%), combining a ~4.5% dividend yield, ~6.4% FCF yield, low PEG (~0.42), and high reported ROE (~39%) against a cyclical consumer-electronics franchise that has stabilised after a multi-year revenue decline. The investment case rests on a capital-light balance sheet, sustained shareholder returns, and early signs of demand recovery tied to product-cycle innovation (computing, gaming, mobile phones), partially validated by a stronger fiscal Q1 2027. The central debate is whether improved comparable sales and earnings mark the start of a durable upgrade cycle, or a temporary relief rally in a structurally challenged big-box model facing Amazon, vendor direct-to-consumer channels, tariff uncertainty, and ongoing Best Buy Health restructuring.
investment_thesis:
The screen flags BBY across five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with passes including FCF Yield, Lynch/Neff PEG variants, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Piotroski F-Score, and Earnings Quality. That profile fits a **value investor seeking income plus cyclical recovery optionality**: the market prices a mature, low-growth retailer cheaply on earnings and cash flow despite a national omnichannel footprint (1,068 stores at fiscal 2026 year-end, per the FY26 10-K body), Geek Squad services, and growing adjacencies (Best Buy Marketplace, Best Buy Ads).

Business quality is mixed but not distressed. Filings describe a purpose-built omnichannel model with centralised merchandising and vendor partnerships; ~25% of Domestic revenue runs through branded credit cards (FY26 10-K risk factors). Interim filings show momentum rebuilding: fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of **$8.9bn** (+1.9% YoY) with **+2.0% comparable sales**, net earnings **$276m**, and diluted EPS **$1.31** versus **$0.95** a year earlier (Q1 FY27 10-Q, filed 5 Jun 2026). Management attributes growth to gaming, computing, mobile phones, and services/membership offerings.

Capital allocation supports the screen's dividend and quality signals. The board maintains a **$0.96** quarterly dividend (Q1 FY27 10-Q); FY26 Yahoo-sourced cash dividends totalled **$801m** with **$273m** of repurchases under a **$5.0bn** authorisation (**$3.0bn** remaining at 2 May 2026, per Q1 FY27 10-Q). Liquidity is adequate: **$1.75bn** cash (2 May 2026), undrawn **$1.25bn** revolver (expires April 2030), and **$500m** / **$650m** notes due 2028/2030 (Q1 FY27 10-Q). No going-concern language appears in available filing extracts.

The screen's elevated ROE and P/B (5.8x) partly reflect a shrunken equity base after impairments and buybacks rather than exceptional organic growth—an important nuance for value investors anchoring on book.
financial_review:
**Data sources and gaps.** The filings index contains two annual 10-Ks (FY25 filed 19 Mar 2025; FY26 filed 18 Mar 2026) and seven interim 10-Qs with bodies. However, both 10-K body extracts are truncated at ~80,000 characters before Item 7 MD&A financial tables; **annual revenue, net earnings, FCF, and balance-sheet totals below are sourced from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo) with filing cross-check where narrative figures appear.** Interim quarterlies are cited from 10-Q body extracts.

**Annual trend (Yahoo fallback).**

| Fiscal year (ended) | Revenue ($m) | Net income ($m) | Diluted EPS | FCF ($m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 2023 (FY23) | 46,298 | 1,419 | 6.29 | 894 |
| Jan 2024 (FY24) | 43,452 | 1,241 | 5.68 | 675 |
| Feb 2025 (FY25) | 41,528 | 927 | 4.28 | 1,392 |
| Jan 2026 (FY26) | 41,691 | 1,069 | 5.04 | 1,258 |

Revenue has fallen ~10% from the FY23 peak, stabilising near **$41.7bn** in FY26 (+0.4% YoY). Net income rebounded to **$1.07bn** in FY26 (+15% YoY) after FY25 was depressed by restructuring and impairment charges. FY25 filings record a **$475m goodwill impairment** on the Best Buy Health reporting unit (FY25 10-K body); FY26 filings reference further Health-related impairments (**$118m** in Q1 FY27 10-Q notes; **$171m** goodwill/intangible impairment in Q3 FY26 10-Q for the quarter ended 1 Nov 2025).

FY26 operating income (Yahoo) was **$1.75bn**; gross margin ~22.5%. Capital expenditure was **$704m**; operating cash flow **$1.96bn**. Balance sheet at Jan 2026 (Yahoo): cash **$1.74bn**, long-term debt **$1.17bn**, total debt **$4.13bn** (includes **$2.97bn** capital lease obligations), shareholders' equity **$2.96bn**.

**Interim trajectory (primary filings).**

- **Q1 FY26** (ended 3 May 2025): Revenue **$8,767m** (−0.9%); comparable sales **−0.7%**; operating income **$219m** (2.5% margin); net earnings **$202m**; EPS **$0.95**. Restructuring charges **$109m** related to Best Buy Health optimisation (Q1 FY26 10-Q).
- **Q2 FY26** (ended 2 Aug 2025): Revenue **$9,438m** (+1.6%); comparable sales **+1.6%**; net earnings **$186m**; EPS **$0.87**. H1 FY26 revenue **$18,205m** (+0.4%); H1 net earnings **$388m** (Q2 FY26 10-Q).
- **Q3 FY26** (ended 1 Nov 2025): Revenue **$9,672m** (+2.4%); comparable sales **+2.7%**; net earnings **$140m** (impairments **$171m**); EPS **$0.66**. Nine-month revenue **$27,877m** (+1.1%); nine-month net earnings **$528m** vs **$810m** prior year (Q3 FY26 10-Q).
- **Q1 FY27** (ended 2 May 2026): Revenue **$8,936m** (+1.9%); comparable sales **+2.0%**; gross profit **$2,102m** (23.5% rate); operating income **$370m** (4.1% margin); net earnings **$276m**; EPS **$1.31** (Q1 FY27 10-Q). Management cited gaming (+38.1% Domestic comparable sales in entertainment), computing, mobile phones, and services. Restructuring credit **$9m** as prior-year Health exit charges lapped.

**Liquidity.** Q1 FY27 10-Q states sources of liquidity are expected to be sufficient for operations, capex, repurchases, dividends, and strategic initiatives. Cash fell seasonally to **$923m** at 1 Nov 2025 before rebuilding to **$1,749m** by 2 May 2026. Nine-month FY26 operating cash flow was **$684m** (Q3 FY26 10-Q). Credit Agreement (April 2025, per Q1 FY26 10-Q exhibit reference) contains customary affirmative and negative covenants; no covenant breach is disclosed in available extracts.

**Controls.** Q1 FY27 10-Q: CEO and CFO concluded disclosure controls were **effective** at 2 May 2026; no material changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter.
risks_and_flags:
**Structural and cyclical.** FY26 10-K risk factors emphasise discretionary consumer-electronics sensitivity to macro conditions, inflation, and tariff/geopolitical disruption. Vendor concentration is acute: top five suppliers (Apple, Samsung, HP, LG, Sony) represented ~**55%** of merchandise purchased; top 20 ~**80%** (FY26 10-K). Heavy Q4 seasonality means a large share of annual profit is concentrated in the holiday quarter.

**Competitive.** Filings warn of price-transparent online competition, vendor direct channels, and AI-driven shopping shifts eroding traffic and margins. Best Buy's service-heavy model carries a higher cost structure than pure-play e-commerce rivals.

**Restructuring and Health.** Multi-year restructuring (store/labor optimisation, Health business exit/impairment) has created earnings volatility. FY25 **$475m** Health goodwill write-down and FY26 further impairments signal strategic retrenchment, not expansion, in healthcare adjacency.

**Balance sheet nuance.** Reported ROE is flattered by a reduced equity base; **P/B 5.8x** on screen metrics is not deep asset-based value. Total debt including leases (~**$4.1bn**) exceeds long-term notes alone; lease-adjusted leverage matters for a big-box retailer closing stores (management guided ~5–10 Domestic store reductions in FY26, with four additional closures expected by end FY27 per Q1 FY27 10-Q).

**Governance / insider activity.** Founder and chairman emeritus Richard Schulze sold approximately **$74m** of stock in July 2026 (news manifest)—not alarming alone at his ownership scale, but worth monitoring alongside reduced buyback activity in Q1 FY27 (no repurchases in the quarter).

**Regulatory / legal.** No material legal proceedings are detailed in 10-Q bodies; contingencies are cross-referenced to notes not extracted here. Tariff policy uncertainty is explicitly flagged as a planning risk in FY26 10-K and Q1 FY27 restructuring disclosures. No going-concern qualification in available filings.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is moderate-to-heavy around earnings and sentiment, with limited deep strategic reporting.

**Earnings and sentiment (material):**
- *Best Buy stock climbs 15% on earnings beat as retailer aims to reinvigorate sales* (CNBC, 28 May 2026) — Q1 FY26 beat drove a sharp relief rally on stronger-than-expected sales, new gadgets, and tax-refund tailwinds.
- *BBY Stock Eyes Best Week In 6 Years After Strong Q1 Fuels Hopes Of A Long-Awaited Electronics Upgrade Cycle* (Stocktwits, 24 Jul 2026).
- *Best Buy (BBY) Stock Fair Value Rises After Q1 Relief Rally And Analyst Revisions* (Yahoo Finance, 18 Jul 2026) — fair-value estimates reportedly shifted toward ~$79.
- *DA Davidson Boosts Best Buy (BBY) Price Objective Following Management Meetings* (Yahoo Finance, 21 Jun 2026).

**Strategy and product:**
- *Best Buy's RGB TV push Is catching fire, Jefferies says* (Yahoo Finance, 15 Jul 2026) — exclusive RGB LED TV positioning cited as a traffic driver.
- *Best Buy names chief fulfillment and operations officer* (Yahoo Finance, 21 Jul 2026) — Duane Scarboro appointed to lead sourcing, supply chain, and delivery.

**Insider and ownership:**
- *Best Buy's Founder and Chairman Emeritus Sold Company Shares Worth $74 Million* (Yahoo Finance, 22 Jul 2026).
- *Best Buy chairman emeritus Schulze sells $74m in BBY stock* (Investing.com, 15 Jul 2026).

**Macro / sector context:**
- *Confidence Is Back, But Earnings Show the Consumer Is Being Picky* (Yahoo Finance, 21 Jul 2026) — uneven spending across income cohorts.
- Amazon Prime Day competitive-promotion coverage (Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026) underscores promotional intensity in consumer electronics.

**Thin or repetitive coverage:** Numerous MarketBeat fund-holding notices and valuation-debate pieces (e.g., Simply Wall St "8% overvalued" vs "reasonable on earnings," Jul 2026) add little incremental fundamental insight.
research_rationale: Deep research largely confirms the screen's strong-buy signal on cash generation, dividend yield, and improving comparable-sales momentum, but tempers conviction given revenue still below pre-2023 peaks, Health-related impairments, vendor/tariff concentration, and the need to rely on Yahoo for full-year figures where 10-K body extracts are truncated.
